metaDescription: Every satellite dataset, forecast, map layer, boundary, library and font behind Emerge, with its licence and a link.
lead: Emerge turns twenty five years of NASA satellite fire detections into one fire record you can read for any place on Earth, and adds an unofficial next-day risk outlook. This page lists everything it is built on.
whatBody: Two families of satellite instruments have watched for fires since November 2000. They see the ground differently, so their counts cannot be compared directly. Emerge puts both on one scale, month by month, and shows the result as a calendar. A separate, unofficial outlook ranks where new fires are most likely tomorrow.
notBody: It is not a warning service. Values before 2012 are estimated from the older instruments and are marked as estimated. The risk outlook is a research prototype tested on past data, not an official forecast.
howLinkBody: Diagrams of the satellites, the conversion, the next-day model and how it compares.
creditsLead: Every outside dataset, service, library and font, as listed in the project's references file. Names and licences are given in each resource's own words.

projectBody: Emerge was built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, at the Sofia local event, for the challenge on harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS hot spots. Its code is open source under the Apache License 2.0. The data keeps its own licences, listed with each source above.
